There will be double or even triple the car, truck, and airplane traffic by 1990 and the noise level will be much greater.
Questioned why the noise measurements were not taken at various times of the day.
Questioned the need for building the Airport Spur just to save three or four minutes.
Car and truck traffic on I-94 will increase by 63% over today's volume while air traffic will increase by 115%. In order for the overall noise in the area to increase by 3 dBA (adding two equal noise sources together increases the noise level by only 3 dBA), car, truck, and air traffic must all increase by 100%.
An increase in traffic and the corresponding increase in noise is based on the assumption that no modification, to cars, trucks, and airplanes which would reduce the noise, will be made. The federal government and private industry, however, are spending millions of dollars a year to reduce noise to acceptable limits.
Federal guidelines require that existing noise levels be measured and future noise levels be predicted at the same time so that a comparison of these levels will show the impact on the area. The Federal guidelines also require that the time of day chosen to measure and predict the noise levels should be the time when the noise levels will be the greatest. The noise levels were, therefore, taken during the morning, midday, and evening rush hours which produce the most traffic and the greatest noise.
In addition to the measurements taken during the peak traffic hours, 24 hours of noise measurements were taken at Hamlin-Garland School and the resulting noise levels are shown on page 122.
See pages 43 thru 45 for the stated needs of this project.
